topIssues.title: Investigate evaluator overhead between independent read actions
topIssues.author: NubsCarson
topIssues.body:
## Follow-up

Nubs will look into this later. This is a deferred optimization investigation, not a confirmed correctness bug or an approved implementation change.

A combined Notes and Calendar read used four foreground model calls: response handler, planner, evaluator after Notes, and the same evaluator again after Calendar. The first evaluation decided whether to continue; the second checked completion and produced the answer.

Investigate whether demonstrably independent, read-only actions can complete before a single evaluation, without weakening conditional execution, permissions, failure handling, evidence checks, or final-answer validation. Do not simply remove the intermediate evaluation: dependent requests may need it to decide whether the next action should run.

Acceptance for any future proposal:
- Explicitly distinguish independent work from conditional or dependent work.
- Preserve cases where the second read must not execute.
- Compare actual trajectories, correctness, call counts, token usage, and latency.
- Retain the existing behavior unless a simpler safe alternative is supported by evidence.

No runtime behavior is changed as part of filing this issue.

topIssues.title: Steer token-address queries return unrelated wallet vaults
topIssues.author: hermesagent270-commits
topIssues.body:
## Problem

The shipped `STEER_LIQUIDITY` wallet provider can report unrelated Steer vaults for a token-address query.

`SteerLiquidityService.getTokenLiquidityStats()` treats any vault with a `poolAddress` as a token match, even when neither `token0` nor `token1` equals the requested address. If an address has no direct matches, the same method then falls back to every vault on the selected chain. The provider renders those vaults under `FOUND ... VAULTS` for the requested token, producing materially incorrect wallet analytics.

## Reproduction

Invoke the production service method with a deterministic Steer SDK boundary containing:

- one vault whose `token0` equals `0xaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
- one unrelated vault with different `token0`/`token1`
- a `poolAddress` on both vaults, matching the real SDK shape

Current result:

```json
{
  "known": [
    "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
    "0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222"
  ],
  "unknown": [
    "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
    "0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222"
  ]
}
```

The known address should return only the first vault. The unknown address should return no vaults.

## Acceptance criteria

- Token-address searches include only vaults whose `token0` or `token1` address equals the requested address, case-insensitively.
- A `poolAddress` alone never proves token membership.
- An explicit token-address query with no matches returns an empty result instead of falling back to all chain vaults.
- Symbol/general overview behavior remains unchanged.
- Regression coverage exercises the public service path for both a matching and an unknown address.

- Migrate monorepo imports, mocks, dynamic types and build aliases together. Remove personal-assistant contract, app automation and UI domain/voice forwarding modules. Native-inference's existing optional local router remains an optional peer, avoiding a UI/provider dependency cycle.

topPRs.title: feat(os): share native OTA trust engine with compiled host policy
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Change
Extract the native OTA trust engine into `packages/os/native/ota-trust`, a pinned Go module shared by Android hosts. It covers TUF verification/rotation, constrained HTTPS, rollback and security-floor admission, rollout scheduling, bounded APK/runtime verification, durable staging, and recovery authorization.

Host identity is explicitly compiled into the signed build through an unexported linker variable: strict base64url JSON with product, package, cohort domain and runtime inventory header. Missing or malformed configuration fails closed. There is no runtime setter and no remote or renderer-selected policy. Existing Senior Care values preserve its deployed cohort and inventory formats; signing authority, trust enrollment, hardware policy, UI and commit authorization remain consumer-owned.

Senior Care removes 21 duplicate production Go files (4,195 lines), consumes byte-identical shared source through a hash-pinned overlay, and keeps local host/toolchain configuration, product admission vectors and instrumentation fixture adapters. Twenty duplicate mechanism test files also move upstream. Generated source composition is content-addressed and rejects altered or extra source files. The original product checkout's pinned upstream submodule is unchanged.

## Validation

- Consumer composed-source `go test -race ./...` passed (177.3 seconds), with the actual compiled product policy.
- Consumer `go vet ./...` passed.

All 15 actual ARM64 JNI instrumentation tests passed with SELinux Enforcing, including positive release admission and packaged-runtime validation. Test packages were removed, HOME preserved, and the temporary read-only emulator shut down. Both ordinary app distributions, instrumentation APK builds, lint and APK identity/HOME checks passed.
